It is submitted that the challan has been filed, the petitioners are in custody since 22.08.2025 and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused-petitioners.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the bail application but he is not in a position to refute the fact that the other co-accused Ajay and Prateek have already been enlarged on bail.

Having heard and considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case as well as perused the material available on record, considering the fact that the offence alleged against the petitioners are triable by the Court of Magistrate, co- accused Ajay and Prateek have already been enlarged on bail, petitioners are in custody since 22.08.2025 and the trial will take significant time to conclude, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioners on bail.
Consequently, the bail application under Section 483 of BNSS (439 of Cr.P.C.) is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused- petitioners as named in the cause title, arrested in connection with the above mentioned FIR, shall be released on bail, if not wanted (Uploaded on 07/11/2025 at 05:49:13 PM) [2025:RJ-JD:47962] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-10833/2025] in any other case, provided each of them furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court, for their appearance before that Court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
(MUKESH RAJPUROHIT),J 376-Ramesh/-
